newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU, South Africa sign Lome deal.
newsitem.headline: EU, South Africa sign Lome deal.

text.p: The European Union and South Africa on Thursday signed a protocol giving South Africa partial access to the Lome convention, the world's largest aid and trade pact, and opening the door to a bilateral free trade accord.

Under the convention, seventy African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) countries -- mainly former French and British colonies -- enjoy privileged access for exports to the 15-nation EU market as well as aid worth $4.0 billion annually.

The protocol, signed for the EU by Dutch Development Minister Jan Pronk and by South African Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom, will allow South African firms to bid for EU-funded projects and Pretoria full political participation.
Negotiations, which began in June 1995, were blocked for many months because of disagreement about the trade elements of the package, mainly over agricultural and wine exports.
The EU, under pressure from its powerful farming lobby, was concerned about South African farm products flooding the market.
South Africa hesitated until December 1996 about whether to negotiate, due to doubts about the potential trade benefits and concern about the possible harmful impact on its neighbours.
The final obstacle was removed last month when Spain lifted its veto linked to concerns over delays in a fisheries deal and worries over imports of South African wine.
